description: Direction Sense question bank for FDA/SDA Mental Ability. Covers Directions; Distance; Position as per supplied syllabus notes. Verify before formal examination use.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What are the four cardinal directions?
questions.explanation: The four cardinal directions are North (N), South (S), East (E), and West (W).

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What are the four intermediate directions?
questions.explanation: The four intermediate directions are North-East (NE), South-East (SE), South-West (SW), and North-West (NW).

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Which direction is opposite North?
questions.explanation: South is opposite to North.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Which direction is opposite South?
questions.explanation: North is opposite to South.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Which direction is opposite East?
questions.explanation: West is opposite to East.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Which direction is opposite West?
questions.explanation: East is opposite to West.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Which direction lies between North and East?
questions.explanation: North-East lies between North and East.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Which direction lies between East and South?
questions.explanation: South-East lies between East and South.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Which direction lies between South and West?
questions.explanation: South-West lies between South and West.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Which direction lies between West and North?
questions.explanation: North-West lies between West and North.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How are directions arranged on a conventional map?

options.A: North at top, South at bottom, East on right, West on left
options.B: North at bottom, South at top, East on left, West on right
options.C: East at top, West at bottom, North on right, South on left
options.D: South at top, North at bottom, West on right, East on left

questions.explanation: On a conventional map, North is at the top, South at the bottom, East on the right, and West on the left. A different orientation must be followed if explicitly given.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a compass?

options.A: A diagram showing cardinal and intermediate directions
options.B: An instrument used to identify direction, traditionally by aligning with the Earth's magnetic field
options.C: A tool used to measure distance
options.D: A device used to measure angles in a triangle

questions.explanation: A compass is an instrument used to identify direction, traditionally by aligning with the Earth's magnetic field.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a direction rose?

options.A: An instrument used to identify direction
options.B: A diagram that displays cardinal and intermediate directions
options.C: A tool used to measure distance travelled
options.D: A method of calculating shortest distance

questions.explanation: A direction rose is a diagram that displays cardinal and intermediate directions.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the angle between two adjacent cardinal directions?
questions.explanation: The angle between two adjacent cardinal directions (e.g., North and East) is 90 degrees.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the angle between a cardinal direction and its adjacent intermediate direction?
questions.explanation: The angle between a cardinal direction and its adjacent intermediate direction (e.g., North and North-East) is 45 degrees.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the angle between North and South?
questions.explanation: North and South are opposite directions, so the angle between them is 180 degrees.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the angle between East and West?
questions.explanation: East and West are opposite directions, so the angle between them is 180 degrees.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a relative direction?

options.A: A fixed compass direction like North or South
options.B: A direction that locates one person or object in relation to another, such as east of a school
options.C: The direction in which a person is facing
options.D: The direction of the shortest path between two points

questions.explanation: A relative direction locates one person or object in relation to another, such as 'east of a school'.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is orientation?

options.A: The shortest distance between two points
options.B: The direction in which a person or object is facing at a particular moment
options.C: The total path covered by a person
options.D: The relative position of an object with respect to a fixed point

questions.explanation: Orientation is the direction in which a person or object is facing at a particular moment.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a right turn?

options.A: An anti-clockwise quarter-turn of 90 degrees from the direction currently faced
options.B: A clockwise quarter-turn of 90 degrees from the direction currently faced
options.C: A turn of 180 degrees to face the opposite direction
options.D: A clockwise turn of 45 degrees from the direction currently faced

questions.explanation: A right turn is a clockwise quarter-turn of 90 degrees from the direction currently faced.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a left turn?

options.A: A clockwise quarter-turn of 90 degrees from the direction currently faced
options.B: An anti-clockwise quarter-turn of 90 degrees from the direction currently faced
options.C: A turn of 180 degrees to face the opposite direction
options.D: An anti-clockwise turn of 45 degrees from the direction currently faced

questions.explanation: A left turn is an anti-clockwise quarter-turn of 90 degrees from the direction currently faced.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a U-turn?

options.C: A turn of 180 degrees that makes a person face the opposite direction

questions.explanation: A U-turn is a 180-degree turn that makes a person face the opposite direction.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a 270-degree clockwise turn equivalent to?
questions.explanation: A 270-degree clockwise turn is equivalent to a 90-degree anti-clockwise turn, which is a left turn.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a 270-degree anti-clockwise turn equivalent to?
questions.explanation: A 270-degree anti-clockwise turn is equivalent to a 90-degree clockwise turn, which is a right turn.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If a person faces North and turns right, which direction is faced?
questions.explanation: A right turn from North (clockwise 90 degrees) leads to East.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If a person faces North and turns left, which direction is faced?
questions.explanation: A left turn from North (anti-clockwise 90 degrees) leads to West.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If a person faces South and turns right, which direction is faced?
questions.explanation: A right turn from South (clockwise 90 degrees) leads to West.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If a person faces South and turns left, which direction is faced?
questions.explanation: A left turn from South (anti-clockwise 90 degrees) leads to East.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If a person faces East and turns right, which direction is faced?
questions.explanation: A right turn from East (clockwise 90 degrees) leads to South.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If a person faces East and turns left, which direction is faced?
questions.explanation: A left turn from East (anti-clockwise 90 degrees) leads to North.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If a person faces West and turns right, which direction is faced?
questions.explanation: A right turn from West (clockwise 90 degrees) leads to North.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If a person faces West and turns left, which direction is faced?
questions.explanation: A left turn from West (anti-clockwise 90 degrees) leads to South.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If a person faces North and makes a U-turn, which direction is faced?
questions.explanation: A U-turn is a 180-degree turn, so facing North becomes facing South.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If a person faces North-East and turns right by 90 degrees, which direction is faced?
questions.explanation: A 90-degree clockwise (right) turn from North-East leads to South-East.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If a person faces North-West and turns left by 90 degrees, which direction is faced?
questions.explanation: A 90-degree anti-clockwise (left) turn from North-West leads to South-West.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Does right always mean East and left always mean West?

options.B: No, right and left depend on the direction currently faced
options.C: Yes, but only when facing North
options.D: No, right always means North and left always means South

questions.explanation: Right and left depend on the current facing direction. Right from North is East, but right from East is South.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the most common mistake in turn questions?

options.A: Adding distances instead of subtracting them
options.B: Treating right as East or left as West regardless of the current facing direction

questions.explanation: The most common mistake is treating right as East or left as West regardless of the current facing direction. The facing direction must be updated after every turn.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.chapter: Direction After a Sequence of Turns
questions.question: How should a sequence of turns be solved?

options.A: Add all turn angles and divide by 90
options.B: Record the initial facing direction, apply each turn in order, and update the facing direction after every turn
options.C: Assume right always means East and left always means West
options.D: Only consider the first and last turns

questions.explanation: Record the initial facing direction, apply each turn in the order given, and update the facing direction after every turn.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.chapter: Direction After a Sequence of Turns
questions.question: A person faces North and turns right twice. Which direction is faced?
questions.explanation: North → East (first right) → South (second right). Final direction: South.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.chapter: Direction After a Sequence of Turns
questions.question: A person faces North, turns left, then right. Which direction is faced?
questions.explanation: North → West (left) → North (right). Final direction: North.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.chapter: Direction After a Sequence of Turns
questions.question: A person faces East and turns left twice. Which direction is faced?
questions.explanation: East → North (first left) → West (second left). Final direction: West.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.chapter: Direction After a Sequence of Turns
questions.question: A person faces South, turns right, then left, then left. Which direction is faced?
questions.explanation: South → West (right) → South (left) → East (left). Final direction: East.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.chapter: Direction After a Sequence of Turns
questions.question: A person faces West and turns right three times. Which direction is faced?
questions.explanation: West → North (right) → East (right) → South (right). Final direction: South.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.chapter: Direction After a Sequence of Turns
questions.question: A person faces North and turns 270 degrees clockwise. Which direction is faced?
questions.explanation: A 270-degree clockwise turn from North is equivalent to a 90-degree anti-clockwise turn, leading to West.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.chapter: Direction After a Sequence of Turns
questions.question: A person faces South-East and turns 180 degrees. Which direction is faced?
questions.explanation: A 180-degree turn from South-East gives the opposite direction, North-West.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.chapter: Direction After a Sequence of Turns
questions.question: A person faces North-East and turns 90 degrees clockwise. Which direction is faced?
questions.explanation: A 90-degree clockwise turn from North-East leads to South-East.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.chapter: Direction After a Sequence of Turns
questions.question: A person faces South-West and turns 90 degrees anti-clockwise. Which direction is faced?
questions.explanation: A 90-degree anti-clockwise turn from South-West leads to South-East.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.chapter: Distance, Total Distance and Shortest Distance
questions.question: What is distance travelled?

options.A: The straight-line change in position from start to finish
options.B: The total length of the actual path covered, irrespective of direction
options.C: The shortest path between two points
options.D: The net displacement in a given direction

questions.explanation: Distance travelled is the total length of the actual path covered, irrespective of direction.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.chapter: Distance, Total Distance and Shortest Distance
questions.question: What is displacement?

options.A: The total length of the actual path covered
options.B: The straight-line change in position from the starting point to the final point, including direction
options.C: The sum of all route segments travelled
options.D: The distance measured along the route without direction

questions.explanation: Displacement is the straight-line change in position from the starting point to the final point, including direction.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.chapter: Distance, Total Distance and Shortest Distance
questions.question: What is the difference between distance and displacement?

options.A: Distance measures straight-line change; displacement measures the complete route
options.B: Distance measures the complete route and is a scalar; displacement measures straight-line change from start to finish and has magnitude and direction
options.C: Both measure the same thing but with different units
options.D: Distance is always less than displacement

questions.explanation: Distance measures the complete route and is a scalar quantity. Displacement measures the straight-line change from start to finish and has magnitude and direction. Distance is never less than the magnitude of displacement.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.chapter: Distance, Total Distance and Shortest Distance
questions.question: What is the shortest distance between the starting and ending points?

options.C: The sum of horizontal and vertical movements

questions.explanation: The shortest distance between the starting and ending points is the straight-line distance between them.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.chapter: Distance, Total Distance and Shortest Distance
questions.question: Which formula is used when horizontal and vertical movements are perpendicular?

options.B: d = √(x² + y²), where x is net horizontal displacement and y is net vertical displacement

questions.explanation: When horizontal and vertical movements are perpendicular, the straight-line distance is d = √(x² + y²), where x is the net horizontal displacement and y is the net vertical displacement.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.chapter: Distance, Total Distance and Shortest Distance
questions.question: A person walks 3 km East and then 4 km North. What is the shortest distance from the start?
questions.explanation: Shortest distance = √(3² + 4²) = √25 = 5 km towards North-East.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.chapter: Distance, Total Distance and Shortest Distance
questions.question: A person walks 6 m North and 8 m East. What is the shortest distance?
questions.explanation: Shortest distance = √(6² + 8²) = √100 = 10 m towards North-East.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.chapter: Distance, Total Distance and Shortest Distance
questions.question: A person walks 5 m East and then 5 m West. Find distance and displacement.

options.B: Distance = 10 m, Displacement = 0 m because the person returns to the starting point

questions.explanation: Distance = 5 + 5 = 10 m. Displacement = 0 m because the person returns to the starting point.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.chapter: Distance, Total Distance and Shortest Distance
questions.question: A person walks 7 km North and then 3 km South. What is the final displacement and total distance travelled?

options.A: Displacement = 4 km North; Total distance = 10 km
options.B: Displacement = 10 km North; Total distance = 4 km
options.C: Displacement = 4 km South; Total distance = 10 km

questions.explanation: Net displacement = 7 − 3 = 4 km North. Total distance travelled = 7 + 3 = 10 km.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.chapter: Distance, Total Distance and Shortest Distance
questions.question: A person walks 9 m East and 12 m South. What is the shortest distance?
questions.explanation: Shortest distance = √(9² + 12²) = √225 = 15 m towards South-East.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.chapter: Distance, Total Distance and Shortest Distance
questions.question: A person walks 10 m North, 6 m East, and 10 m South. Where is the person relative to the start?
questions.explanation: The North and South movements cancel (10 − 10 = 0). The net movement is 6 m East.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.chapter: Distance, Total Distance and Shortest Distance
questions.question: A person walks 4 m West, 3 m South, 4 m East, and 3 m North. Where does the person finish?
questions.explanation: Net horizontal displacement = 4 West − 4 East = 0. Net vertical displacement = 3 South − 3 North = 0. The person finishes at the starting point.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.chapter: Distance, Total Distance and Shortest Distance
questions.question: What is the 3-4-5 right-triangle rule?

options.A: A right triangle with perpendicular sides 3 and 4 units has a hypotenuse of 5 units; multiples include 6-8-10 and 9-12-15
options.B: A triangle with sides 3, 4, and 6 units
options.C: A right triangle with hypotenuse 3 units and sides 4 and 5 units

questions.explanation: A right triangle with perpendicular sides 3 and 4 units has a hypotenuse of 5 units. Multiples include 6-8-10 and 9-12-15.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.chapter: Distance, Total Distance and Shortest Distance
questions.question: What is the 5-12-13 right-triangle rule?

options.A: A right triangle with perpendicular sides 5 and 12 units has a hypotenuse of 13 units
options.B: A triangle with sides 5, 12, and 15 units
options.C: A right triangle with hypotenuse 5 units and sides 12 and 13 units

questions.explanation: A right triangle with perpendicular sides 5 and 12 units has a hypotenuse of 13 units.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.chapter: Distance, Total Distance and Shortest Distance
questions.question: Can total distance and shortest distance be equal?

options.B: Yes, when the person travels along a straight line without changing direction
options.C: Yes, only when the person returns to the starting point
options.D: Yes, only when the person travels in a circle

questions.explanation: Total distance and shortest distance can be equal when the person travels along a straight line without changing direction.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is position in direction-sense reasoning?

options.A: The total distance travelled by a person
options.B: The location of a person or object relative to a reference point, such as north of a building or south-east of a park
options.C: The direction a person is facing
options.D: The shortest path between two points

questions.explanation: Position is the location of a person or object relative to a reference point, such as north of a building or south-east of a park.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How is the final position found after several movements?

options.A: By adding all distances travelled regardless of direction
options.B: By combining all East-West movements to find net horizontal displacement and all North-South movements to find net vertical displacement, then using the final signs to identify the quadrant
options.C: By taking the average of all movements
options.D: By using only the last movement

questions.explanation: Combine all East-West movements to find net horizontal displacement and all North-South movements to find net vertical displacement. Use the final signs to identify the quadrant.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If the net movement is East and North, in which direction is the final point?
questions.explanation: Net movement East and North places the final point in the North-East direction.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If the net movement is West and North, in which direction is the final point?
questions.explanation: Net movement West and North places the final point in the North-West direction.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If the net movement is East and South, in which direction is the final point?
questions.explanation: Net movement East and South places the final point in the South-East direction.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If the net movement is West and South, in which direction is the final point?
questions.explanation: Net movement West and South places the final point in the South-West direction.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If only East-West movement remains after cancellation, what is the final direction?

options.C: East or West, depending on which movement is greater

questions.explanation: If only East-West movement remains after cancellation, the final direction is East or West, depending on which movement is greater.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If only North-South movement remains after cancellation, what is the final direction?

options.C: North or South, depending on which movement is greater

questions.explanation: If only North-South movement remains after cancellation, the final direction is North or South, depending on which movement is greater.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If net horizontal and vertical movements are both zero, where is the final position?
questions.explanation: If net horizontal and vertical movements are both zero, the final position is at the starting point.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What does 'A is north of B' mean?

options.A: A is located north of B; equivalently, B is south of A
options.B: A is located south of B; equivalently, B is north of A
options.C: A and B are at the same position

questions.explanation: 'A is north of B' means A is located north of B; equivalently, B is south of A.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If A is east of B, where is B relative to A?
questions.explanation: If A is east of B, then B is west of A.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If P is south of Q and Q is east of R, where is P relative to R?
questions.explanation: Q is east of R, and P is south of Q. Therefore P is south-east of R.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: A school is west of a hospital and a bank is north of the school. Where is the bank relative to the hospital?
questions.explanation: The bank is north of the school, and the school is west of the hospital. So the bank is north-west of the hospital (assuming positions on the same simple direction grid).

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the difference between 'left of B' and 'west of B'?

options.B: Left is relative to the direction B is facing; West is a fixed compass direction. They are equivalent only when B faces North
options.C: Left is a fixed compass direction; West is relative to B's facing

questions.explanation: Left is relative to the direction B is facing; West is a fixed compass direction. They are equivalent only when B faces North.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the conventional Sun-direction rule used in aptitude questions?

options.A: The Sun rises in the West and sets in the East
options.B: The Sun is treated as rising in the East and setting in the West
options.C: The Sun is always in the North
options.D: The Sun is always directly overhead

questions.explanation: The Sun is treated as rising in the East and setting in the West. Actual sunrise and sunset positions vary seasonally, but standard aptitude questions use this simplified rule.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: In the morning, if a person faces the rising Sun, which direction is the person facing?
questions.explanation: The Sun rises in the East, so a person facing the rising Sun faces East.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: In the evening, if a person faces the setting Sun, which direction is the person facing?
questions.explanation: The Sun sets in the West, so a person facing the setting Sun faces West.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: In the morning, in which direction does a person's shadow generally fall?
questions.explanation: In the morning, the Sun is conventionally treated as being in the East, so the shadow falls towards the West.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: In the evening, in which direction does a person's shadow generally fall?
questions.explanation: In the evening, the Sun is conventionally treated as being in the West, so the shadow falls towards the East.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If a person faces East in the morning, where is the shadow?

options.A: East, in front of the person

questions.explanation: In the morning, the shadow falls towards the West. If the person faces East, the shadow is West, behind the person.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If a person's shadow falls behind them in the evening, which direction are they facing under the conventional assumption?
questions.explanation: The evening shadow is East; if it is behind the person, the person faces the opposite direction, West.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What caution is necessary in shadow questions?

options.A: Always assume the shadow falls North
options.B: Use the time of day and any direction explicitly stated; do not assume a shadow is always North or South
options.C: Always assume the shadow falls South

questions.explanation: Use the time of day and any direction explicitly stated. Do not assume a shadow is always North or South.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: A person walks 8 m North, turns right, and walks 6 m. How far and in which direction is the person from the start?
questions.explanation: A right turn from North is East. Net movement is 8 m North and 6 m East. Shortest distance = √(8² + 6²) = 10 m, towards North-East.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: A person walks 12 m East, 5 m North, and 12 m West. Find the final position.

options.A: 5 m North of the starting point
options.B: 5 m South of the starting point
options.C: 12 m East of the starting point

questions.explanation: East and West movements cancel (12 − 12 = 0). The person is 5 m North of the starting point.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: A person faces South, turns left, walks forward, and then turns right. Which direction is faced at the end?
questions.explanation: South → East after the left turn; East → South after the right turn. Final facing direction: South.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: A person walks 10 m North, 10 m East, 10 m South, and 5 m West. Find the final position and shortest distance.
questions.explanation: North and South cancel (10 − 10 = 0). Net horizontal movement = 10 East − 5 West = 5 m East. Final position and shortest distance: 5 m East.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: A person walks 5 km West and 12 km North. Find the shortest distance and direction.
questions.explanation: Shortest distance = √(5² + 12²) = √169 = 13 km, towards North-West.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: A person faces North and turns 135 degrees clockwise. Which direction is faced?
questions.explanation: A 135-degree clockwise turn from North is one 90-degree turn to East plus 45 degrees to South-East.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: A is 4 km North of B. C is 3 km East of A. Where is C relative to B and what is the straight-line distance?
questions.explanation: C is 3 km East and 4 km North of B, i.e., North-East, at a straight-line distance of √(3² + 4²) = 5 km.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: A person walks 7 m South, turns left, and walks 4 m. What is the final direction from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Facing South, left is East. The person is 7 m South and 4 m East of the start: South-East.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.chapter: Common Exam Traps and Error Checks
questions.question: Why should the starting direction be written before solving a turn problem?

options.B: Left and right are relative to the current facing direction; recording the starting direction prevents incorrect assumptions
options.C: To determine the total distance travelled
options.D: To find the final position directly

questions.explanation: Left and right are relative to the current facing direction. Recording the starting direction prevents incorrect assumptions.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.chapter: Common Exam Traps and Error Checks
questions.question: Why must a route be traced in the exact order given?

options.A: Because distances must be added in order
options.B: Each turn changes the facing direction, so the next turn depends on the direction reached after the previous turn
options.C: Because the shortest distance depends on the order
options.D: Because the starting point changes with each turn

questions.explanation: Each turn changes the facing direction, so the next turn depends on the direction reached after the previous turn.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.chapter: Common Exam Traps and Error Checks
questions.question: Why is final facing direction different from final location?

options.B: Facing direction describes where a person looks; location describes where the person stands relative to the start. A person can face North while standing South-East of the start
options.C: Facing direction is always opposite to location
options.D: Location is measured only after the final turn

questions.explanation: Facing direction describes where a person looks; location describes where the person stands relative to the start. A person can face North while standing South-East of the start.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.chapter: Common Exam Traps and Error Checks
questions.question: Does walking 5 m North and then 5 m South mean zero distance travelled?

options.B: No, total distance is 10 m, but displacement is zero
options.C: Yes, both distance and displacement are zero

questions.explanation: Total distance is 10 m, but displacement is zero because the person returns to the starting point.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.chapter: Common Exam Traps and Error Checks
questions.question: Can a person finish North-East of the starting point while facing South?

options.B: Yes, final location and final facing direction are separate
options.C: Yes, but only after a U-turn
options.D: No, facing direction always matches location

questions.explanation: Yes. Final location and final facing direction are separate.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.chapter: Common Exam Traps and Error Checks
questions.question: What should be done if a diagram gives a non-standard North direction?

options.A: Ignore the diagram and use page North
options.B: Follow the orientation explicitly given in the diagram, not the usual page convention
options.C: Rotate the diagram to match page North
options.D: Assume North is always at the top of the page

questions.explanation: Follow the orientation explicitly given in the diagram, not the usual page convention.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.chapter: Common Exam Traps and Error Checks
questions.question: What should be done when asked for shortest distance after a route?

options.B: Find net horizontal and vertical displacements, then use the straight-line distance formula if both components are non-zero
options.C: Use only the first and last segments
options.D: Multiply the horizontal and vertical displacements

questions.explanation: Find net horizontal and vertical displacements, then use the straight-line distance formula if both components are non-zero.

questions.subject: Mental Ability

questions.question: If only East-West movement remains after cancellation, what is the final direction?

options.B: East or West, depending on which movement is greater

questions.explanation: If only East-West movement remains, the final direction is East or West depending on which movement is greater.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If only North-South movement remains after cancellation, what is the final direction?

options.B: North or South, depending on which movement is greater

questions.explanation: If only North-South movement remains, the final direction is North or South depending on which movement is greater.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If net horizontal and vertical movements are both zero, where is the final position?
questions.explanation: When both net displacements are zero, the final position is at the starting point.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What does 'A is north of B' mean?

options.A: A is located north of B; equivalently, B is south of A
options.C: A and B are at the same place

questions.explanation: 'A is north of B' means A is located north of B; equivalently, B is south of A.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If A is east of B, where is B relative to A?
questions.explanation: If A is east of B, then B is west of A.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If P is south of Q and Q is east of R, where is P relative to R?
questions.explanation: Q is east of R and P is south of Q, so P is south-east of R.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: A school is west of a hospital and a bank is north of the school. Where is the bank relative to the hospital?
questions.explanation: The school is west of the hospital; the bank is north of the school. So the bank is north-west of the hospital.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the difference between 'left of B' and 'west of B'?

options.B: Left is relative to the direction B is facing; West is a fixed compass direction. They are equivalent only when B faces North
options.C: West is relative and left is fixed

questions.explanation: Left depends on the direction B is facing, while West is a fixed compass direction. They coincide only when B faces North.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the conventional Sun-direction rule used in aptitude questions?

options.A: The Sun rises in the West and sets in the East
options.B: The Sun is treated as rising in the East and setting in the West
options.C: The Sun is always in the North

questions.explanation: In standard aptitude questions, the Sun is treated as rising in the East and setting in the West (actual positions vary seasonally).

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: In the morning, if a person faces the rising Sun, which direction is the person facing?
questions.explanation: The Sun rises in the East, so a person facing the rising Sun faces East.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: In the evening, if a person faces the setting Sun, which direction is the person facing?
questions.explanation: The Sun sets in the West, so a person facing the setting Sun faces West.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: In the morning, in which direction does a person's shadow generally fall?
questions.explanation: In the morning the Sun is in the East, so shadows fall West.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: In the evening, in which direction does a person's shadow generally fall?
questions.explanation: In the evening the Sun is in the West, so shadows fall East.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If a person faces East in the morning, where is the shadow?

options.A: East, in front of the person

questions.explanation: Morning shadows fall West. If the person faces East, the West shadow is behind the person.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If a person's shadow falls behind them in the evening, which direction are they facing under the conventional assumption?
questions.explanation: The evening shadow is East. If it is behind the person, the person faces the opposite direction, West.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What caution is necessary in shadow questions?

options.A: Assume a shadow is always North or South
options.B: Use the time of day and any direction explicitly stated; do not assume a shadow is always North or South
options.D: Always assume the Sun is overhead

questions.explanation: Use the time of day and any direction explicitly stated. Do not assume a shadow is always North or South.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: A person walks 8 m North, turns right, and walks 6 m. How far and in which direction is the person from the start?
questions.explanation: A right turn from North is East. Net movement is 8 m North and 6 m East. Shortest distance = √(8² + 6²) = 10 m, towards North-East.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: A person walks 12 m East, 5 m North, and 12 m West. Find the final position.
questions.explanation: East and West movements cancel (12 − 12 = 0). The person is 5 m North of the starting point.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: A person faces South, turns left, walks forward, and then turns right. Which direction is faced at the end?
questions.explanation: South → East (left turn); East → South (right turn). Final facing direction: South.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: A person walks 10 m North, 10 m East, 10 m South, and 5 m West. Find the final position and shortest distance.
questions.explanation: North and South cancel. Net horizontal movement = 10 − 5 = 5 m East. Final position and shortest distance: 5 m East.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: A person walks 5 km West and 12 km North. Find the shortest distance and direction.
questions.explanation: √(5² + 12²) = 13 km. West and North give the North-West direction.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: A person faces North and turns 135 degrees clockwise. Which direction is faced?
questions.explanation: A 135° clockwise turn from North is one 90° turn to East plus 45° to South-East.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: A is 4 km North of B. C is 3 km East of A. Where is C relative to B and what is the straight-line distance?
questions.explanation: C is 3 km East and 4 km North of B, i.e., North-East. Straight-line distance = √(3² + 4²) = 5 km.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: A person walks 7 m South, turns left, and walks 4 m. What is the final direction from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Facing South, left is East. The person is 7 m South and 4 m East of the start: South-East.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.chapter: H. Common Exam Traps and Error Checks
questions.question: Why should the starting direction be written before solving a turn problem?

options.B: Left and right are relative to the current facing direction; recording the starting direction prevents incorrect assumptions

questions.explanation: Left and right depend on the current facing direction, so recording the starting direction prevents incorrect assumptions.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.chapter: H. Common Exam Traps and Error Checks
questions.question: Why must a route be traced in the exact order given?

options.B: Each turn changes the facing direction, so the next turn depends on the direction reached after the previous turn
options.C: Because the shortest distance depends on order

questions.explanation: Each turn changes the facing direction, so the next turn depends on the direction reached after the previous turn.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.chapter: H. Common Exam Traps and Error Checks
questions.question: Why is final facing direction different from final location?

options.B: Facing direction describes where a person looks; location describes where the person stands relative to the start. A person can face North while standing South-East of the start
options.D: Facing direction is measured from the start

questions.explanation: Facing direction is where the person looks; location is where the person stands relative to the start. They are independent.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.chapter: H. Common Exam Traps and Error Checks
questions.question: Does walking 5 m North and then 5 m South mean zero distance travelled?

options.B: No; total distance is 10 m, but displacement is zero
options.C: Yes, both distance and displacement are zero

questions.explanation: Total distance is 10 m, but displacement is zero because the person returns to the start.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.chapter: H. Common Exam Traps and Error Checks
questions.question: Can a person finish North-East of the starting point while facing South?

options.B: Yes; final location and final facing direction are separate

questions.explanation: Final location and final facing direction are separate; a person can stand North-East of the start while facing South.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.chapter: H. Common Exam Traps and Error Checks
questions.question: What should be done if a diagram gives a non-standard North direction?

options.A: Use the usual page convention (top = North)
options.B: Follow the orientation explicitly given in the diagram, not the usual page convention
options.D: Assume North is always at the top

questions.explanation: Follow the orientation explicitly given in the diagram, not the usual page convention.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.chapter: H. Common Exam Traps and Error Checks
questions.question: What should be done when asked for shortest distance after a route?

options.B: Find net horizontal and vertical displacements, then use the straight-line distance formula if both components are non-zero

questions.explanation: Find net horizontal and vertical displacements, then apply d = √(x² + y²) if both components are non-zero.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: A person faces East and turns left. Which direction is faced?
questions.explanation: A left turn from East (anti-clockwise 90°) gives North.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: A person faces West and turns left. Which direction is faced?
questions.explanation: A left turn from West (anti-clockwise 90°) gives South.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: A person faces South and turns right twice. Which direction is faced?
questions.explanation: South → West (right) → North (right). Final direction: North.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: A person faces North-East and makes a 180-degree turn. Which direction is faced?
questions.explanation: A 180° turn makes the person face the opposite direction: North-East → South-West.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: A person walks 4 m North and 3 m East. What is the shortest distance?

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: A person walks 9 m South and 12 m West. What is the shortest distance and direction?
questions.explanation: √(9² + 12²) = √225 = 15 m. South and West give the South-West direction.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: A person walks 15 m East and 8 m West. Where is the person relative to the start?
questions.explanation: Net movement = 15 − 8 = 7 m East.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: A person walks 11 m North and 6 m South. Where is the person relative to the start?
questions.explanation: Net movement = 11 − 6 = 5 m North.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: A person walks 5 m East, 5 m North, 5 m West, and 5 m South. Where does the person finish and what are the total distance and displacement?

options.A: At the starting point; total distance 20 m; displacement 0 m
options.B: 5 m North; total distance 20 m; displacement 5 m
options.C: At the starting point; total distance 0 m; displacement 20 m
options.D: 5 m East; total distance 20 m; displacement 5 m

questions.explanation: East-West and North-South movements cancel, so the person finishes at the starting point. Total distance = 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 = 20 m; displacement = 0 m.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: A person faces South and turns left twice. Which direction is faced?
questions.explanation: South → East (left) → North (left). Final direction: North.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: A person faces East and turns right three times. Which direction is faced?
questions.explanation: East → South (right) → West (right) → North (right). Final direction: North.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: A person walks 6 km West and 8 km South. What is the shortest distance?
questions.explanation: √(6² + 8²) = √100 = 10 km. West and South give the South-West direction.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: A is east of B. B is north of C. Where is A relative to C?
questions.explanation: B is north of C and A is east of B, so A is north-east of C.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: A is west of B. C is south of B. Where is A relative to C?
questions.explanation: A is west of B and C is south of B, so A is north-west of C.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: A is 6 km South of B and C is 8 km West of A. Where is C relative to B and what is the straight-line distance?
questions.explanation: C is 6 km South and 8 km West of B, i.e., South-West. Straight-line distance = √(6² + 8²) = 10 km.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If a person faces the rising Sun, which direction is behind the person?
questions.explanation: Facing the rising Sun means facing East; behind the person is West.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: In the evening, a person's shadow falls behind them. Which direction are they facing under the conventional rule?
questions.explanation: The evening shadow falls East. If East is behind the person, the person faces West.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: A person starts facing North, turns 90° clockwise, then 180° anti-clockwise. Which direction is faced?
questions.explanation: North → East (90° clockwise); a 180° anti-clockwise turn from East gives West.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: A person travels 3 m North, 4 m East, 3 m South, and 4 m West. What is the final displacement?

options.A: Zero; the person returns to the starting point

questions.explanation: North-South cancel (3 − 3 = 0) and East-West cancel (4 − 4 = 0). Displacement is zero; the person returns to the start.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: A person is 5 km North of a library. In which direction is the library from that person?
questions.explanation: If the person is north of the library, the library is south of the person.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Which pair of directions is opposite to each other?

options.B: North ↔ South; East ↔ West; North-East ↔ South-West; North-West ↔ South-East

questions.explanation: Opposite pairs: North ↔ South; East ↔ West; North-East ↔ South-West; North-West ↔ South-East.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the rule for a right turn?
questions.explanation: A right turn is a clockwise 90° turn from the current facing direction.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the rule for a left turn?
questions.explanation: A left turn is an anti-clockwise 90° turn from the current facing direction.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the formula for shortest distance when net movements are perpendicular?
questions.explanation: For perpendicular net movements, shortest distance d = √(x² + y²).

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How is net East-West displacement calculated?
questions.explanation: Net East-West displacement = East distance − West distance.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How is net North-South displacement calculated?
questions.explanation: Net North-South displacement = North distance − South distance.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How is total distance calculated in a route problem?

options.B: Add every segment travelled; do not cancel opposite movements

questions.explanation: Total distance is found by adding every segment travelled; opposite movements are not cancelled.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is displacement?

options.A: The sum of all segments travelled
options.B: The straight-line change from starting point to final point
options.C: The direction faced at the end

questions.explanation: Displacement is the straight-line change from the starting point to the final point.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: According to the final exam checklist, what should be kept separate while solving a direction problem?
questions.explanation: The checklist states: keep facing direction separate from final position.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: According to the final exam checklist, when should opposite movements be cancelled?

options.D: Always, for both distance and displacement

questions.explanation: Cancel opposite movements only when finding net displacement; add all segments for total distance.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: According to the final exam checklist, when is the Pythagorean theorem used?

options.B: For perpendicular net movements to find shortest distance

questions.explanation: Use the Pythagorean theorem for perpendicular net movements to find the shortest distance.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Which direction is opposite to South?
questions.explanation: North is opposite South.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Which direction is opposite to West?
questions.explanation: East is opposite West.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Which direction lies between East and South?
questions.explanation: South-East lies between East and South.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Which direction lies between West and North?
questions.explanation: North-West lies between West and North.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the angle between East and West?
questions.explanation: East and West are opposite directions, so the angle between them is 180 degrees.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.chapter: C. Direction After a Sequence of Turns
questions.question: A person faces South-West and turns 90 degrees clockwise. Which direction is faced?
questions.explanation: A 90° clockwise turn from South-West gives North-West.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.chapter: C. Direction After a Sequence of Turns
questions.question: A person faces North-West and turns 90 degrees anti-clockwise. Which direction is faced?
questions.explanation: A 90° anti-clockwise turn from North-West gives South-West.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.chapter: C. Direction After a Sequence of Turns
questions.question: A person faces South-East and turns 90 degrees anti-clockwise. Which direction is faced?
questions.explanation: A 90° anti-clockwise turn from South-East gives North-East.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If a person faces South and makes a U-turn, which direction is faced?
questions.explanation: A U-turn is 180°, so from South the person faces North.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: A person walks 6 km North, 4 km East, and 6 km South. Where is the person relative to the start?
questions.explanation: North and South cancel (6 − 6 = 0), leaving 4 km East.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: A person walks 8 km South and 15 km West. What is the shortest distance from the start?
questions.explanation: √(8² + 15²) = √289 = 17 km. South and West give the South-West direction.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: A person walks 9 km North and 12 km East. What is the shortest distance from the start?
questions.explanation: √(9² + 12²) = √225 = 15 km. North and East give the North-East direction.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: A person faces West, turns right, and then turns left. Which direction is faced?
questions.explanation: West → North (right) → West (left). Final direction: West.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.chapter: H. Common Exam Traps and Error Checks
questions.question: How can sign errors be avoided in long routes?

options.B: Assign consistent signs to East-West and North-South movements and combine them carefully
options.C: Add all movements as positive values
options.D: Use only the first and last segments

questions.explanation: Assign consistent signs (e.g., East +, West −, North +, South −) and combine carefully to avoid sign errors in long routes.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: In the morning, a person's shadow falls in front of them. Which direction are they facing?
questions.explanation: Morning shadows fall West. If the shadow is in front, the person faces West's opposite, i.e., East.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: If Q is west of P and R is south of Q, where is R relative to P?
questions.explanation: Q is west of P and R is south of Q, so R is south-west of P.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: A person facing North turns 90° anti-clockwise, then 270° clockwise. Which direction is faced?
questions.explanation: North → West after the 90° anti-clockwise turn. A 270° clockwise turn equals three 90° clockwise turns: West → North → East → South. Final direction: South.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: A person walks 20 m North, then 15 m South, then 10 m North. What is the final displacement and total distance?
questions.explanation: Net North-South = 20 − 15 + 10 = 15 m North. Total distance = 20 + 15 + 10 = 45 m.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: A temple is south of a lake. A shop is east of the temple. Where is the shop relative to the lake?
questions.explanation: The temple is south of the lake and the shop is east of the temple, so the shop is south-east of the lake.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.chapter: C. Direction After a Sequence of Turns
questions.question: A person faces North, turns 45° clockwise, then 90° anti-clockwise. Which direction is faced?
questions.explanation: North → North-East after 45° clockwise; North-East → North-West after 90° anti-clockwise. Final direction: North-West.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: A person walks 3 km North, 4 km East, 6 km South, and 8 km West. What is the shortest distance from the start and in which direction?
questions.explanation: Net North-South = 3 − 6 = 3 km South. Net East-West = 4 − 8 = 4 km West. Shortest distance = √(3² + 4²) = 5 km. South and West give the South-West direction.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.chapter: H. Common Exam Traps and Error Checks
questions.question: A person walks 4 km North, turns right and walks 3 km. They then turn right and walk 4 km. Where are they relative to the start?
questions.explanation: 4 km North; right turn (East) 3 km; right turn (South) 4 km. North and South cancel, leaving 3 km East.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: In the evening, a person walks facing away from their shadow. Which direction are they walking?
questions.explanation: Evening shadows fall East. Facing away from the shadow means facing West.
